title: U.S.-Brokered Talks Yield Major Russia-Ukraine POW Swap, But Peace Remains Out of Reach
snippet: Negotiators in Abu Dhabi reached an agreement in principle for a massive prisoner exchange, but fundamental disputes over security and territory continue to stall broader peace efforts.
content:
ABU DHABI — Following two days of intensive, U.S.-mediated negotiations in the United Arab Emirates, Russian and Ukrainian delegates have agreed in principle to conduct their largest prisoner-of-war exchange since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion nearly five years ago.

Despite the humanitarian milestone, envoys acknowledged that the high-stakes summit in Abu Dhabi yielded no breakthrough toward ending the war. Deep divisions remain over the fate of Russian-occupied Ukrainian territory, postwar security guarantees, and the framework for future diplomatic talks.

Diplomatic Push Moves to Moscow and Dublin

The Abu Dhabi session marked the first direct encounter between delegation leaders in nine months. U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff mediated the trilateral discussions, working alongside Russian delegation chief Vladimir Medinsky and Ukrainian chief negotiator Rustem Umerov.

Following the conclusion of the talks on Wednesday, Kushner announced that he and Witkoff would travel to Moscow to meet directly with Russian President Vladimir Putin before flying to Dublin to consult with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

“One of the positives is we agreed that we’re going to have the biggest humanitarian release of prisoners,” Kushner told reporters, noting that final numbers for the exchange were being finalized.

Friction Over European Participation

A central point of contention during the summit was the role of European nations. Moscow blocked European diplomats from attending the primary three-way negotiations, forcing Ukrainian representatives to meet separately with officials from the European Union, NATO, and individual European governments who had traveled to the UAE capital.

Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov justified the stance by criticizing European arms shipments to Kyiv, asserting that current statements from European leaders do not indicate a real willingness to contribute to peace. Conversely, Kushner stressed that durable security arrangements require consensus among NATO and European allies, stating that integrating European leaders into future rounds of talks remains a priority for his mission in Moscow.

Fighting Escalates Ahead of Further Talks

The diplomatic maneuverings took place against the backdrop of sustained violence across the combat zone. Ukrainian authorities reported that a daytime Russian strike targeted a marketplace in the southern Odesa region, killing three people and injuring 11. Heavy aerial attacks also struck Kharkiv and Zaporizhzhia overnight.

Simultaneously, Ukrainian forces launched extensive drone strikes deep inside Russian territory. Moscow's Defense Ministry reported shooting down over 600 drones, including a barrage near St. Petersburg that ignited a fire at the Ust-Luga oil export terminal, a key hub for Russian energy exports.

With military positions largely stalled on the front lines and mutual trust nonexistent, diplomats face a formidable challenge in turning temporary humanitarian agreements into a comprehensive ceasefire.
